We are happy to announce that we have been shortlisted for four awards at this year's Constructing Excellence South West Awards!

Our TBY2 Studios (Hawkfield) project, which was procured through SCF Frameworks, has been named a finalist in three different categories, with the Building Project of the Year and the Value award, plus the Client of the Year award for Bristol City Council.  The project has seen Bristol City Council (BCC) and ISG deliver a sustainable facility to support Bristol’s thriving film/tv industry while leaving a social legacy for the community.

The Pathfinder scheme is a first for the DfE, with a unique collaboration between ISG, DfE, Bath and North East Somerset Local Authority and Futura Learning Partnership which saw the design and construction of the school.

Congratulations to all those involved, and good luck to all those shortlisted.

The AWE has appointed Mace as Manufacturing Programme Partner for a major infrastructure development programme. Mace has been appointed in partnership with BakerHicks and DBD International. 

The purpose of this complex, long term programme is to develop a new component manufacturing capability to support the United Kingdom’s nuclear deterrent. As Manufacturing Programme Partner, Mace, BakerHicks and DBD will work in partnership with AWE over the next decade to support the delivery of new manufacturing facilities. 

Jason Millett, Mace’s CEO for Consultancy, said: 

"This programme is one of the most ambitious and challenging defence infrastructure programmes being delivered in Europe. It will require the delivery of cutting-edge manufacturing facilities, working in one of the most complex live environments anywhere in our industry."

Today Mace is launching our new 2026 Business Strategy; outlining a radical vision of a more sustainable and inclusive business model; and setting ourselves bold targets that will shape our next five years.

Our purpose sits at the heart of our new strategy. It’s why we exist. It’s what drives us forward. It’s how we create an enduring legacy in this world: to redefine the boundaries of ambition.

Over the next five years, we aim to fundamentally transform how the built environment is developed, delivered and operated. Our targets will see us deliver 90% of our projects with modern methods of construction by 2026, reduce our carbon emissions by 10% year-on-year and maintain our Net Zero status.

Alongside this, we have set ourselves ambitious new growth goals that will see us achieve £3bn in annual revenue and employ more than 8,000 people by 2026.

Our strength as a business has always been our exceptional people and their industry-defining ambition and expertise. By setting out our purpose and priorities clearly, we want to put our colleagues at the centre of everything we do.

Together, we want to redefine the boundaries of ambition.
